disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: Anglo-Saxons & Vikings
root.gloss: How Angles, Saxons, Jutes, and Scandinavian Vikings raided, settled, traded, and fought from AD 410 to forge one Kingdom of England before 1066.

children.label: 1. Saxon Settlers & Monks
children.gloss: Angles, Saxons, and Jutes rowed across the North Sea to build timber mead-hall kingdoms, buried royal ship treasures at Sutton Hoo, and embraced Christian monasteries.

children.label: 1. Angles, Saxons & Jutes Settle
children.q2Chain: Flooded marshes push & rich farms pull across North Sea → West Stow villages & mead halls → Seven kingdoms & Old English words
children.gloss: Flooded marshes push & rich farms pull across North Sea → West Stow villages & mead halls → Seven kingdoms & Old English words

children.label: North Sea Push & Pull Boats
children.gloss: Flooded coastal marshes pushed Angles, Saxons, and Jutes out while Britain’s fertile farmland pulled families across in oak rowing boats.

children.label: Flooded Marshes vs Rich Farmland
children.gloss: Tides ruined Jutland, Saxony crops; Unguarded river valleys after 410.

children.label: Families Rowed Nydam Oak Ships
children.gloss: Packed seeds, livestock, iron tools; Steered up eastern English rivers.

children.label: → Cleared New Timber Farmsteads
children.gloss: Settled Angles, Saxons, and Jutes; Built villages beside clear streams.

children.label: West Stow & Timber Mead Halls
children.gloss: Avoiding ruined Roman stone towns, free ceorls wove wool at West Stow around a warrior king’s roaring timber mead hall.

children.label: Ceorls Built Thatched West Stow
children.gloss: Called Roman walls giants’ work; Wove wool; forged iron tools.

children.label: Cyning Shared Mead & Gold Rings
children.gloss: Grand rectangular timber mead hall; Roaring hearth, honey mead, rings.

children.label: → Grew Into Seven Rival Kingdoms
children.gloss: Loyal fighters guarded regional kings; Joined warbands into wider realms.

children.label: Seven Kingdoms & Weekday Gods
children.gloss: Rival warbands formed the seven-kingdom Heptarchy, giving England its name, -ham/-ton/-ford towns, and four pagan weekday names.

children.label: Seven Kingdoms Named Englaland
children.gloss: Northumbria, Mercia, Wessex, Kent, Essex; East Anglia, Sussex spoke Old English.

children.label: East Anglia, Sussex spoke Old English
children.gloss: East Anglia, Sussex spoke Old English

children.label: Place-Names & Pagan Weekdays
children.gloss: -ham, -ton, -ford dot maps; Tiw, Woden, Thunor, Frige weekdays.

children.label: Shaped England’s Map & Speech
children.gloss: Meant land of the Angles; Spoken roots survive every day.

children.label: 2. Sutton Hoo & Monasteries
children.q2Chain: King Raedwald’s 27m Sutton Hoo ship burial → Missionaries at Canterbury (597) & Lindisfarne (635) → Lindisfarne Gospels & Bede
children.gloss: King Raedwald’s 27m Sutton Hoo ship burial → Missionaries at Canterbury (597) & Lindisfarne (635) → Lindisfarne Gospels & Bede

children.label: Sutton Hoo’s 27m Ghost Ship
children.gloss: In 1939 on Edith Pretty’s Suffolk land, Basil Brown uncovered rusted iron rivets and royal treasures of King Raedwald.

children.label: Iron Rivets Traced 27m Ship
children.gloss: Basil Brown dug Mound 1; Acidic sand rotted oak planks.

children.label: Helmet, Garnets & Silver Spoons
children.gloss: Famous iron-and-bronze war helmet; Sri Lankan garnets, Byzantine spoons.

children.label: Crossroads of Pagan & Christian
children.gloss: Honoured King Raedwald c. AD 625; Proved rich global Saxon trade.

children.label: Canterbury & Lindisfarne Monks
children.gloss: Christianity arrived from two directions: Augustine at Canterbury in AD 597 and Irish monk Aidan from Iona at Lindisfarne in AD 635.

children.label: AD 597: Augustine at Canterbury
children.gloss: Sent by Pope Gregory in Rome; Welcomed by Ethelbert, Queen Bertha.

children.label: Sent by Pope Gregory in Rome
children.gloss: Sent by Pope Gregory in Rome

children.label: AD 635: Aidan Founded Lindisfarne
children.gloss: Sailed south from island Iona; Built priory beside King Oswald.

children.label: → Monasteries Spread Books & Art
children.gloss: Baptised kings north and south; Built peaceful coastal stone priories.

children.label: Whitby, Vellum Gospels & Bede
children.gloss: Abbess Hilda united church rules at Whitby, scribes painted calfskin vellum Gospels, and Bede wrote English history at Jarrow.

children.label: Abbess Hilda & Vellum Quills
children.gloss: Hosted AD 664 Whitby Synod; Painted Lindisfarne Gospels on vellum.

children.label: Venerable Bede’s AD 731 History
children.gloss: Wrote at Jarrow monastery scriptorium; Spread AD dates across Europe.

children.label: → Rich Priories Tempted Sea Raiders
children.gloss: Filled churches with silver, gold; Left island Lindisfarne unguarded.

children.label: 2. Viking Longships & Alfred
children.gloss: Shallow-draught Viking longships struck Lindisfarne in AD 793 and conquered three kingdoms before King Alfred won at Edington, agreed the Danelaw, and built 33 burhs.

children.label: 3. Longships & Heathen Army
children.q2Chain: Dragon prows raid Lindisfarne (8 June 793) → Clinker-built 1m-draught longships → Great Heathen Army conquers Jorvik (865–877)
children.gloss: Dragon prows raid Lindisfarne (8 June 793) → Clinker-built 1m-draught longships → Great Heathen Army conquers Jorvik (865–877)

children.label: AD 793: Raid on Lindisfarne
children.gloss: On 8 June AD 793, Scandinavian raiders in dragon-prowed warships stormed unguarded Lindisfarne Priory for silver and gold.

children.label: Unguarded Priory Held Rich Silver
children.gloss: Gold reliquaries and unarmed monks; Isolated coastal Holy Island target.

children.label: 8 June 793 Shocked All Europe
children.gloss: Chronicle warned of fiery dragons; Scholar Alcuin wept in terror.

children.label: → Launched 70 Years of Raids
children.gloss: Raiders sailed from Norway, Denmark; Exposed Britain’s open sea coasts.

children.label: Clinker-Built Oak Longships
children.gloss: Overlapping oak strakes, tarred wool, square sails, oars, and a 1-metre shallow draught let Viking crews row straight up rivers.

children.label: Overlapping Oak & Tarred Wool
children.gloss: Held tight by iron rivets; Pointed ends reversed off beaches.

children.label: Wool Sail, Oars & 1m Draught
children.gloss: Crossed stormy open North Sea; Rowed far up English rivers.

children.label: → Carried Huge Conquest Armies
children.gloss: Surprised inland monasteries and towns; Enabled AD 865 winter invasion.

children.label: AD 865: Great Heathen Army
children.gloss: Craving fertile farmland, the AD 865 Great Heathen Army wintered at Repton and seized York (Jorvik), East Anglia, and Mercia.

children.label: Scandinavian Farmland Ran Short
children.gloss: Mountainous Norway and sandy Denmark; Chieftains craved new kingdoms.

children.label: Ivar, Halfdan & Guthrum Seize York
children.gloss: Built winter camp at Repton; Captured Jorvik in AD 866.

children.label: → Only Wessex Stood by AD 877
children.gloss: Took East Anglia and Mercia; Pushed King Alfred into marshes.

children.label: 4. Alfred, Burhs & The Danelaw
children.q2Chain: Athelney marshes to Edington victory (AD 878) → Guthrum baptised & Danelaw treaty → 33 walled burhs, 60-oar ships & schools
children.gloss: Athelney marshes to Edington victory (AD 878) → Guthrum baptised & Danelaw treaty → 33 walled burhs, 60-oar ships & schools

children.label: Athelney Marshes to Edington
children.gloss: After Guthrum’s surprise attack at Chippenham, King Alfred hid at Athelney before rallying the fyrd to smash Guthrum at Edington.

children.label: Twelfth Night Raid on Chippenham
children.gloss: Guthrum struck Wessex Jan 878; Alfred hid in Somerset marshes.

children.label: Fyrd Shield Wall Won Edington
children.gloss: Cheered Alfred at Egbert’s Stone; Smashed Vikings in May 878.

children.label: → Forced Guthrum’s Peace Treaty
children.gloss: Saved last free Saxon kingdom; Surrounded Guthrum surrendered camp.

children.label: Baptism & The Danelaw Border
children.gloss: Guthrum was baptised as Christian Aethelstan, Alfred retook London, and their treaty split England along Roman Watling Street.

children.label: Guthrum Baptised as Aethelstan
children.gloss: Alfred stood as Christian godfather; Recaptured walled London AD 886.

children.label: Watling Street Split the Danelaw
children.gloss: Alfred held Wessex, west Mercia; Vikings ruled -by, -thorpe Danelaw.

children.label: → Gave Breathing Space for Burhs
children.gloss: Minted King of English pennies; Bought time to fortify Wessex.

children.label: 33 Burhs, Ships & Saxon Books
children.gloss: Alfred built 33 walled burhs within 20 miles of every village, launched 60-oar warships, and translated Latin books into Old English.

children.label: 33 Walled Burhs & 60-Oar Ships
children.gloss: Wareham, Wallingford earth ramparts; Safety within twenty miles everywhere.

children.label: Court Schools & Alfred Jewel
children.gloss: Translated Latin into Old English; Started famous Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

children.label: Earned Title “Alfred the Great”
children.gloss: Paired school learning with swords; Laid base for united England.

children.label: 3. Jorvik Life, Unity & 1066
children.gloss: Archaeology under York’s Coppergate revealed global Viking traders and craftworkers before Aethelflaed and Athelstan united England and 1066 brought Norman rule.

children.label: 5. Everyday Viking Jorvik
children.q2Chain: 40,000 finds preserved in Coppergate peat → Silk, Baghdad dirhams & Atlantic knarrs → Women’s keys, Thing courts & Old Norse words
children.gloss: 40,000 finds preserved in Coppergate peat → Silk, Baghdad dirhams & Atlantic knarrs → Women’s keys, Thing courts & Old Norse words

children.label: 40,000 Finds Under Coppergate
children.gloss: Wet oxygen-free peat beneath York’s Coppergate preserved timber workshops, leather shoes, bone ice-skates, and antler combs.

children.label: Wet Airless Peat Saved Wood
children.gloss: Dug beneath York 1976–1981; Stopped leather and wood rotting.

children.label: Shoes, Skates & Antler Combs
children.gloss: Bone skates and hnefatafl counters; Hundreds of deer-antler combs.

children.label: Proved Vikings Were Skilled Makers
children.gloss: Cared about neat daily hygiene; Far more than fierce raiders.

children.label: Baghdad Silver & Ocean Knarrs
children.gloss: Jorvik imported Byzantine silk, Red Sea shells, and Baghdad silver dirhams while wide knarr cargo ships sailed to North America.

children.label: Silk, Amber & Baghdad Dirhams
children.gloss: Byzantine silk, Red Sea cowrie; Traded furs for Arabic dirhams.

children.label: Knarr Ships Reached Vinland
children.gloss: Steered across icy North Atlantic; Reached Iceland, Greenland, and Vinland.

children.label: Linked York Across Three Continents
children.gloss: Linked York, Baghdad, and Vinland; Made Jorvik a bustling port.

children.label: Keys, Thing Courts & Old Norse
children.gloss: Danelaw wives wore household keys and owned land, outdoor Thing assemblies voted on laws, and Old Norse gave us everyday words.

children.label: Karls, Thralls & Key-Bearing Wives
children.gloss: Free karls farmed; thralls laboured; Women owned land, could divorce.

children.label: Outdoor Things & Norse Words
children.gloss: Voted laws at Thing assemblies; Gave sky, window, egg, knife.

children.label: → Blended Into One English Nation
children.gloss: Settlers wed Saxons, turned Christian; Added husband and Thursday too.

children.label: 6. Aethelflaed, Athelstan & 1066
children.q2Chain: Aethelflaed & Athelstan unite England (911–937) → Danegeld, Cnut’s Empire & Edward → Stamford Bridge & Hastings (Oct 1066)
children.gloss: Aethelflaed & Athelstan unite England (911–937) → Danegeld, Cnut’s Empire & Edward → Stamford Bridge & Hastings (Oct 1066)

children.label: Aethelflaed & King Athelstan
children.gloss: Lady of the Mercians Aethelflaed recaptured Derby and Leicester before her nephew Athelstan took York (927) and won Brunanburh (937).

children.label: Aethelflaed Built Mercian Burhs
children.gloss: Fortified Tamworth and Warwick burhs; Recaptured Viking Derby and Leicester.

children.label: Athelstan Took York & Brunanburh
children.gloss: Captured Viking York AD 927; Won Brunanburh battle AD 937.

children.label: → First True King of All England
children.gloss: United Saxon and Danelaw lands; Created one Kingdom of England.

children.label: Danegeld, King Cnut & Edward
children.gloss: After Aethelred’s silver Danegeld bribes failed, Danish King Cnut ruled a peaceful North Sea Empire before Edward built Westminster Abbey.

children.label: Danegeld Silver Failed to Stop Raids
children.gloss: Fresh Danish fleets struck 991; Raiders returned wanting more silver.

children.label: Cnut’s Empire & Westminster Abbey
children.gloss: Cnut ruled England, Denmark, Norway; Edward opened Westminster Abbey 1065.

children.label: → Childless Death Sparked 1066
children.gloss: Edward died childless January 1066; Three rivals claimed one crown.

children.label: Stamford Bridge & Hastings 1066
children.gloss: Harold Godwinson marched north to crush Viking Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge, then south to fall against William at Hastings.

children.label: 25 Sept: Won Stamford Bridge
children.gloss: Witan crowned Earl Harold Godwinson; Marched 185 miles; beat Hardrada.

children.label: 14 Oct: Shield Wall Fell at Hastings
children.gloss: Exhausted troops marched 250 miles; Duke William’s Normans won crown.

children.label: Ended Viking & Saxon Eras
children.gloss: Stamford Bridge ended Viking Age; Hastings began Norman rule.
